evidence: Duffinian exception is gcd(pq,σ(pq))>1, equivalently p|q+1. Resultary 15a95ebe2dc2 treats exactly this predicate with an O(x/log x) exception bound. Resultary 05d9813b37ff treats gcd(pq,φ(pq))>1, equivalently p|q−1.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: At odd p the progression conditions differ, e.g. (p,q)=(3,5) qualifies only for q+1; (3,7) only for q−1. Neither theorem is an equivalent restatement of the asymptotic for the Duffinian set.

value.rationale: The exception count is naturally motivated but the exact leading constant here is a routine residue substitution in the earlier noncyclic semiprime calculation. That proof already establishes the exact same sum: replacing +1 with −1 keeps the reduced-class main term and BT bound and changes the integer upper bound by at most one per modulus. The only small endpoint case is q=2 at p=3; the p=2 class is identical. The Duffinian local criterion was already established, and no new invariant value, quantified error, or additional distribution information survives this transfer.
